## Load libraries and establish settings

```{r}
# Turn off scientific notation
options(scipen=999)

library(tidyverse)

```

## Load Data

Let's keep working with the UMD courses and Maryland campaign expense data we used in the pre_lab.

```{r}
umd_courses <- read_rds("data/umd_courses.rds")
maryland_expenses <- read_csv("data/maryland_expenses.csv")
```

## Answer questions

**Q1.** How many departments have offered the courses with "Climate" in the title and at least one seat? Which department has offered the most? **A1. 32 departments have offered one or more courses that fulfill the above requirements. The department of Atmospheric and Oceanic Science offered the most with 93.**

```{r}
umd_courses |>
  filter(str_detect(title, "Climate")) |>
  filter (seats >=1) |>
  group_by(department) |>
  summarise(
    courses = n()
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(courses))
```

**Q2.** Of the departments listed in A1, which one is the most interesting to you, and why? **A2. I'm surprised the journalism department offered a course with this constraint. While environmental reporting is consistent with Merrill's goals, I did not expect the word "climate" to appear.**

**Q3** Which departments offered the most courses in the Fall 2024 term? And which departments in that term have at least one syllabus posted? Answer both of those questions and then compare the top five departments - how are they different?

**A3. The departments that offered the most courses in the given term were Business and Management, School of Music and Information Studies. The departments with the most courses that posted a syllabus are similar but have some changes.**

```{r}
umd_courses |>
  filter (term == 202408) |>
  group_by(department) |>
  summarise (
    courses = n()
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(courses))
```

```{r}
umd_courses |>
  filter (term == 202408) |>
  filter (syllabus_count >= 1) |>
  group_by(department) |>
  summarise (
    courses = n()
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(courses))
```

**Q4.** Using the Maryland campaign expenses data, change the datatype of the expenditure_date column so that it is a date and not a chr, saving the result as a new dataframe. Then create a new column for the month based on expenditure_date. Then write code that shows total amount spent each month by Wes Moore's committee (you'll need to search the data to find the exact name, and we're not looking in payee_name). Write a sentence describing the pattern of spending over time. **A4. The spending generally increased over time and peaked shortly prior to the election.**

```{r}
maryland_expenses <- maryland_expenses |> mutate (new_expenditure_date=mdy(expenditure_date))
wes_moore <- maryland_expenses |> filter (str_detect(committee_name, "Wes For"))
wes_moore |>
  mutate(month = floor_date(new_expenditure_date, "month")) |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarise(total_amount = sum(amount)) |>
  arrange(month)
```

**Q5.** Using case_when(), create a column in the Maryland expenses data called `spending_location` indicating whether each record spent money in Maryland or outside Maryland. For records that are in Maryland, make the new column's value "In-state" and for all others, make it "Out of state". Then write code that shows the total amount of money spent in each category and describe the results. You can do this in one statement or break it up into two statements (saving the new column to your dataframe). **A5 The code separates the money between in-state and out-of-state donations. In-state donations are significantly higher as expected.**

```{r}
maryland_expenses_with_state <- maryland_expenses |>
  mutate(
    spending_location = case_when(
      str_detect(address, " Maryland ") ~ "in-state",
      str_detect(address, " California ") ~ "out of state",
      str_detect(address, " Washington ") ~ "out of state",
      str_detect(address, " Louisiana ") ~ "out of state",
      str_detect(address, " Florida ") ~ "out of state",
      str_detect(address, " North Carolina ") ~ "out of state",
      str_detect(address, " Massachusetts ") ~ "out of state",
      str_detect(address, " West Virginia ") ~ "out of state",
      str_detect(address, " Virginia ") ~ "out of state",
      .default = NA
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(spending_location) |>
  summarise(
    total_amount = sum(amount)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(total_amount))
```

**Q6.** Choose your own adventure: using either the UMD courses or campaign expenses data, ask and answer a question that is different than the previous ones. You can use one of the ones you provided in the pre_lab. **A6. Question: How many classes are offered at each level in the Spring 2025 term? (100, 200, etc)**

**The most classes by far were offered at the 400 level in this term.**

```{r}
umd_courses |>
  mutate(level = str_sub(id, start=5, end=5)) |>
  filter (term == 202501) |>
  group_by(level) |>
  summarise (
    courses = n()
  )

  
```
